name: FC Prishtina
content:
FC Prishtina is a professional football club based in Pristina, Kosovo, and competes in the Kosovo Superleague. Founded in 1922, it is one of the oldest clubs in the country and widely regarded as the most successful in Kosovar football history. The team plays its home matches at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium and has built a strong reputation for consistency, having never been relegated from the top division.

The club’s history reflects the broader political and sporting developments in the region. Originally founded as Kosova, it went through several name changes before becoming Prishtina. During the Yugoslav era, the team competed in the national league system and reached the top tier, achieving notable success in the 1980s. In the 1990s, amid political tensions, the club participated in the unofficial independent league in Kosovo before transitioning into the modern Kosovar football system after the war.

FC Prishtina has won numerous domestic titles, including multiple league championships, national cups, and super cups, making it the most decorated club in Kosovo. In recent years, it has also represented the country in European competitions, becoming one of the first Kosovar teams to record victories in UEFA tournaments. The club enjoys strong support from its fan base, particularly the “Plisat” ultras group, which plays an important role in its identity and atmosphere.

name: KF Trepça
content:
KF Trepça is a professional football club based in the southern part of Mitrovica, Kosovo. Founded in 1932, it is one of the oldest and historically significant clubs in the country. The team currently competes in the First Football League of Kosovo, the second tier of the national system, and plays its home matches at the Adem Jashari Olympic Stadium.

The club achieved notable success during the Yugoslav era, becoming the first team from Kosovo to reach the top division of Yugoslav football in the 1977–78 season after winning the second division. In that same period, Trepça reached the final of the Yugoslav Cup, an exceptional achievement for a Kosovar club, although they finished as runners-up. Alongside Prishtina, it was one of the few clubs from Kosovo to compete at the highest level of Yugoslav football.

KF Trepça has also been successful domestically, winning multiple league titles and a national cup, and is considered one of the traditional clubs in Kosovo. Its identity is closely tied to the Trepça mining complex, reflected in its nickname “The Miners.” Despite changes in league status over time, the club remains an important part of Kosovo’s football heritage.

name: KF Dukagjini
content:
KF Dukagjini is a professional football club based in the town of Klina, Kosovo. Founded in 1958, the club competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the highest level of football in the country. It plays its home matches at the 18 June Stadium and is known by the nickname “Hithat” (The Nettles), reflecting its resilient and combative identity.

For much of its history, Dukagjini was a modest club that spent long periods in lower divisions. Its most notable early success came during the 1990s, when it won the title in the independent Kosovo league in the 1993–94 season. The club also reached several domestic cup finals, establishing itself as a respected team within Kosovo’s developing football structure.

In recent years, KF Dukagjini has grown in prominence, becoming a competitive side in the top division. A strong league finish allowed the club to qualify for European competition for the first time, participating in the UEFA Europa Conference League qualifiers in 2023–24. Although still developing compared to Kosovo’s leading clubs, Dukagjini continues to build its reputation through steady progress and community support.

name: KF Liria
content:
KF Liria Prizren is a professional football club based in Prizren, Kosovo. Founded in 1930, it is one of the oldest and most traditional clubs in the country. The team currently competes in the First Football League of Kosovo, the second tier of the national system, and plays its home matches at the Përparim Thaçi Stadium.

The club has a long and complex history shaped by regional and political changes. During the Yugoslav era, Liria competed in the Kosovo Province League and occasionally reached higher divisions. In the early 1990s, it played an important role in the independent Kosovo football system, even participating in the first official match of that competition. The club won its only Kosovo top-division title in the 1994–95 season, marking its peak domestic success.

KF Liria has also achieved success in cup competitions, winning the Kosovar Cup twice and maintaining a strong presence in domestic football over the decades. Although it has experienced periods of relegation and promotion, the club remains an important part of Kosovo’s football heritage. It is supported by a passionate fan base known as “Arpagjik’t,” which contributes to its identity and local rivalry culture.

name: KF Besiana
content:
KF Besiana was a football club based in Podujevo, Kosovo. Founded in 1984, it competed in various levels of the Kosovar football system, including the top division and later the second tier, Liga e Parë. The club was associated with the city also known as Besiana and played its home matches at a local municipal stadium.

The most successful period in the club’s history came during the 2001–02 season, when KF Besiana achieved a remarkable domestic treble. In that campaign, the team won the Kosovo Superleague, the Kosovar Cup, and the Kosovar Super Cup, marking the only major trophies in its history. The club’s colors were yellow and navy blue, and it developed local rivalries with nearby teams such as KF Llapi.

Despite its early success, the club later declined and spent time in lower divisions. It eventually withdrew from league competition and is no longer active in professional football. Nevertheless, KF Besiana remains notable in Kosovo’s football history, particularly for its standout 2001–02 season and its connection to former Kosovo football legend Fadil Vokrri, who was among its founders.

name: FC Drita
content:
FC Drita is a professional football club based in Gjilan, Kosovo, founded in 1947. The club competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the top tier of football in the country, and is one of the most prominent teams in Kosovar football. Its name, meaning “light” in Albanian, reflects its local identity, and the team plays its home matches at the Gjilan City Stadium.

The club’s history has been shaped by political and social changes in the region. In its early years, Drita faced challenges and was even dissolved in 1952 before later re-emerging and achieving success in regional competitions, including winning the Kosovo Province League in 1962–63. During the 1990s, amid the breakup of Yugoslavia, the club participated in Kosovo’s parallel football system, continuing to operate under difficult conditions.

In the modern era, FC Drita has become one of the leading clubs in Kosovo, winning multiple league titles, including championships in 2002–03, 2017–18, and 2019–20. The team has also made steady progress in European competitions, achieving historic milestones such as reaching advanced qualifying rounds and even the later stages of the UEFA Europa Conference League. These achievements have strengthened its reputation as a competitive and ambitious club in the region.

name: FC Besa Peja
content:
FC Besa Peja is a professional football club based in Peja, Kosovo. Founded in 1923, it is one of the oldest football clubs in the country and plays its home matches at the Shahin Haxhiislami Stadium. The team currently competes in the lower tiers of the Kosovo football league system after experiencing fluctuations between divisions over the years.

The club has a long and complex history, originally founded under a different name before evolving into its current identity through mergers and structural changes. During different periods, especially after World War II and following the breakup of Yugoslavia, Besa played in various regional and national competitions. In the post-war era, the club was rebuilt and became an important representative of football in the city of Peja.

Besa Peja enjoyed its greatest success in the mid-2000s, winning three consecutive Kosovo Superleague titles from 2004 to 2007, as well as multiple domestic cup trophies. Despite later financial difficulties that led to temporary dissolution and reformation, the club remains a notable part of Kosovo’s football history, recognized for its achievements and contribution to the development of the sport in the region.

name: KF Hysi
content:
KF Hysi was a professional football club based in Podujevo, Kosovo. Founded in 2002, the club competed in the Kosovo Superleague, the top tier of football in the country, and played its home matches at the Stadiumi Merdar. It was known for being backed by the Hysi Group, making it one of the few privately owned clubs in Kosovo’s top division.

The club rose quickly through the football system, earning promotion to the top division during the 2005–06 season. KF Hysi achieved its greatest success in the late 2000s and early 2010s, winning the Kosovar Cup in 2008–09 and securing the Kosovo Superleague title in the 2010–11 season. These achievements established it as a competitive force in domestic football despite its relatively short history.

However, the club’s success was short-lived. Due to financial difficulties, KF Hysi withdrew from competition and ceased operations in 2014 after leaving the league mid-season. Although it existed for just over a decade, the club remains notable in Kosovo’s football history for its rapid rise and major domestic trophies.

name: FC Vushtrria
content:
FC Vushtrria is a professional football club based in Vushtrri, Kosovo. Founded in 1922, it is the oldest football club in the country and has played an important role in the development of Kosovar football. The team competes in the Kosovo First Football League and plays its home matches at the Ferki Aliu Stadium.

Throughout its history, Vushtrria has been known for developing talented players who later moved on to stronger clubs in Kosovo and abroad. During the Yugoslav era and later periods, the club remained an important football institution in its region, despite not always competing at the highest level. Its strong youth system helped produce several well-known Kosovar internationals, contributing significantly to national football growth.

One of the club’s biggest achievements came in the 2013–14 season, when FC Vushtrria won its first Kosovo Superleague title. This success marked the peak of the club’s modern era and remains its most important trophy. Despite later fluctuations in performance and league status, Vushtrria continues to be recognized as a historic and traditional club in Kosovo football.

name: FC Feronikeli 74
content:
FC Feronikeli 74 is a professional football club based in Drenas, Kosovo. It was originally founded in 1974 under the name Nikeli and later became closely linked with the local mining and metallurgical industry, which influenced both its identity and development. The club is one of the more recognizable teams in Kosovar football and plays its home matches at the Rexhep Rexhepi Stadium.

The club experienced its most successful period in the 2010s after rising through the domestic system. Feronikeli won its first Kosovo Superleague title in the 2014–15 season and went on to secure another championship in 2018–19. During this successful era, the team also collected domestic cup trophies and established itself as one of the strongest sides in the country.

Following its peak, the club faced financial and sporting difficulties, which led to a decline in performance and eventual relegation from the top division. Despite these setbacks, FC Feronikeli 74 remains an important part of Kosovo’s football landscape, known for its rapid rise, championship success, and contribution to the development of the sport in the region.

name: KF Trepça '89
content:
KF Trepça ’89 is a professional football club based in Mitrovica, Kosovo. The club was originally founded in 1940 under different names and was later re-established in 1989, which is reflected in its current name. It competes in the Kosovo football league system and plays its home matches at the Riza Lushta Stadium.

The club has a long history of development through several identities, including Rudari and Minatori ’89, before becoming Trepça ’89. Its name is closely linked to the Trepça mining complex and the local working-class identity of Mitrovica. Over time, the club became one of the more stable and competitive sides in Kosovo football, regularly participating in the top division.

Trepça ’89 achieved its greatest success in the 2016–17 season when it won the Kosovo Superleague title for the first time in its history. This victory also earned the club a place in European competition, where it represented Kosovo in UEFA qualifiers. Despite later ups and downs in performance, the club remains an important part of the country’s football landscape and is known for its historic championship achievement.

name: FC Ballkani
content:
FC Ballkani is a professional football club based in Suhareka, Kosovo, founded in 1947. Originally established under the name Rinia, the club later adopted its current name in 1965 when it became associated with the local industrial company “Ballkan.” It competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the top tier of football in the country, and plays its home matches at the Theranda City Stadium.

For much of its history, Ballkani developed gradually through the Yugoslav league system and later the Kosovo football structure. The club has long been known for its strong local identity and steady progress rather than early dominance. After the Kosovo football system stabilized, Ballkani became a consistent presence in the top division and eventually grew into a competitive side capable of challenging for titles.

The club’s modern era is defined by its rise to the top of Kosovar football. Ballkani won its first Kosovo Superleague title in the 2021–22 season and went on to defend its championship in the following years, establishing itself as one of the strongest teams in the country. It also made history in European competitions by becoming the first Kosovan club to reach the group stage of a UEFA club tournament, marking a major milestone for both the club and national football.

name: KF Flamurtari
content:
KF Flamurtari is a professional football club based in Pristina, Kosovo. Founded in 1968, it is one of the well-known clubs in the capital city and has traditionally been considered one of the stronger teams in Kosovar football. The club plays its home matches at the Xhemail Ibishi Stadium and has spent most of its history competing in the top two tiers of the national league system.

Throughout its history, Flamurtari has been an established presence in domestic competitions. The club has participated in the Kosovo Superleague and has also spent periods in the second division, with fluctuating results over different eras. One of its notable achievements includes reaching the final of the Kosovar Cup in the 2006–07 season, where it finished as runner-up.

In addition to cup success, KF Flamurtari has also won the Kosovar Cup twice in the 1990s, which remains a key part of its historical achievements. Despite not consistently competing for major titles in recent years, the club remains an important part of Pristina’s football landscape, known for its local identity and long-standing presence in Kosovar football.

name: KF Llapi
content:
KF Llapi is a professional football club based in Podujevë, Kosovo, founded in 1932, making it one of the oldest clubs in the country. The team competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the top tier of national football, and plays its home matches at the Zahir Pajaziti Stadium. Over its long history, the club has become an important representative of football in northern Kosovo and has contributed significantly to the development of the sport in the region.

The club spent much of its early and mid-history developing within the Yugoslav football system and later the Kosovo league structure. A major turning point came in 2013, when the club was reorganized with a new management project aimed at professionalizing its structure and returning it to top-level competition. This restructuring helped Llapi become more stable and competitive in domestic football.

In modern times, KF Llapi has established itself as a strong contender in Kosovo football, regularly competing in the Superleague and achieving notable domestic success. The club has also won major trophies, including the Kosovar Cup and the Super Cup, and has participated in UEFA competitions, representing Kosovo on the European stage. These achievements have strengthened its reputation as one of the country’s leading clubs in recent years.

name: FC 2 Korriku
content:
FC 2 Korriku is a professional football club based in Pristina, Kosovo. It was founded in 1957 under the name Proleteri and later renamed 2 Korriku in 1990, a name that refers to “2 July” and is linked to an important historical date in Kosovo’s modern history. The club competes in the Kosovo football league system and plays its home matches at the Fusha Sportive 2 Korriku. It is especially known for its strong identity within the capital city and its long-standing presence in local football.

A defining feature of the club is its football academy, which has become one of the most influential youth development systems in Kosovo. Since its establishment in the early 1990s, the academy has produced many talented players who later progressed to top domestic clubs and international careers. This focus on youth development has made FC 2 Korriku an important contributor to the growth of Kosovar football beyond its own competitive results.

In terms of achievements, FC 2 Korriku has had moments of success in domestic competitions, including winning the Kosovar Cup in the 1995–96 season. While it has not been a dominant force in the top division, the club remains respected for its consistency, player development, and contribution to the football ecosystem in Kosovo. Its role is often seen more in shaping future talent than in collecting major trophies.

name: SC Gjilani
content:
SC Gjilani is a professional football club based in Gjilan, Kosovo. Founded in 1995, the club competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the top division of football in the country. It plays its home matches at the Gjilan City Stadium and is one of the two major clubs from the city, forming part of one of Kosovo’s most intense football rivalries with FC Drita.

The club was established in difficult post-conflict conditions and is considered the successor of earlier football traditions in the city dating back to the mid-20th century. Despite its relatively recent formal foundation, Gjilani quickly established itself in Kosovo football. Within five years of its creation, the club achieved significant success, including winning the Kosovar Cup and earning promotion to the top division, where it has remained a regular competitor.

In modern times, SC Gjilani has become a stable and competitive team in Kosovo’s top flight, often challenging for European qualification places. The club is also known for its passionate supporters group, “Skifterat,” and for its strong derby atmosphere against FC Drita, which is one of the most popular football fixtures in the country. Over time, Gjilani has built a reputation as a resilient club with a strong local identity and consistent presence in elite Kosovar football.

name: FC KEK-u
content:
FC KEK-u is a professional football club based in Obiliq, Kosovo. The club was founded in 1928 and is closely connected with the Kosovo Energy Corporation, which also inspired its name. It competes in the Kosovo First Football League and plays its home matches at the Agron Rama Stadium. The team is known by the nickname “The Electricians,” reflecting its industrial background and identity.

Throughout its history, KEK-u has experienced several name changes and structural transformations, especially during different political periods in the region. The club has competed in various tiers of football in Kosovo and also took part in the Yugoslav league system under earlier names. One of its notable achievements came in the early 2000s when it won domestic cup competitions and briefly competed in the top division.

In recent years, FC KEK-u has mostly played in the second tier of Kosovar football, aiming to stabilize its performance and rebuild competitiveness. The club is known for its long history and resilience rather than consistent top-level success. Despite fluctuations in form and league status, it remains a recognized part of Kosovo’s football landscape and continues to develop players locally.

name: KF Kosova VR Prishtinë
content:
KF Kosova VR Prishtinë is a football club based in the Vranjevc area of Pristina, Kosovo. The club was originally founded in 1946 under the name KF Kosova Prishtinë and later rebranded to its current identity. It competes in the lower tiers of the Kosovo football league system and plays its home matches at the Bërnica Synthetic Grass Stadium. The club is known for its long local tradition within the capital city’s football scene.

Historically, the club has gone through several structural changes and name adjustments, reflecting different periods of Kosovo’s football development. It has participated in various domestic competitions since its formation and has experienced both amateur and semi-professional phases. Despite operating mostly outside the top division in modern times, the club has maintained continuity and remains active in national league structures.

One of its notable achievements includes winning domestic honours in earlier periods, including league and cup success during different eras of competition. The club is also recognized for its long-standing presence in Pristina football and for contributing to the local sporting community. Although it is not currently among the strongest teams in Kosovo, KF Kosova VR Prishtinë retains historical significance due to its longevity and role in developing football in the region.

name: KF Vëllaznimi
content:
KF Vëllaznimi Gjakovë is a professional football club based in Gjakova, Kosovo. Founded in 1927, it is one of the oldest clubs in the country and has a long-standing tradition in Kosovar football. The team currently competes in the Kosovo First Football League, the second tier of the national system, and plays its home matches at the Gjakova City Stadium. The club is often associated with strong local identity and its nickname reflects its connection to the city’s supporters.

Historically, Vëllaznimi is considered one of the most successful clubs in Kosovo, especially during the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s when it dominated the regional Kosovo Province League. During that era, it won multiple league titles and established itself as a major force in Yugoslav-era regional competitions. It also competed in the wider Yugoslav football system before the political changes in the region reshaped football structures in Kosovo.

In more recent decades, the club has experienced fluctuations in performance, moving between divisions and struggling to return to its former dominance. However, it remains an important and historic football institution in Kosovo, with a strong fan base in Gjakova. Vëllaznimi continues to be recognized for its tradition, longevity, and contribution to the development of football in the region.

name: FC Ferizaj
content:
FC Ferizaj is a professional football club based in the city of Ferizaj, Kosovo. Founded in 1923, it is one of the oldest football clubs in the country and has played an important role in the development of Kosovar football. The team competes in the Kosovo First Football League and plays its home matches at the Ismet Shabani Stadium.

Throughout its history, the club has gone through various competitive levels within the domestic football system, including spells in the Kosovo Superleague. Ferizaj has often been seen as a club that develops local talent and provides a platform for players to progress to higher levels of competition. Its identity is strongly tied to the city it represents and its long-standing football tradition.

In recent years, FC Ferizaj has experienced fluctuations in performance, moving between divisions and working to stabilize its position in national competitions. Despite these challenges, the club remains a recognized name in Kosovo football, known for its history, resilience, and contribution to the sport at both local and national levels.

name: FC Hajvalia
content:
FC Hajvalia is a former professional football club based in the village of Hajvalia, near Pristina, Kosovo. Founded in 1999, the club competed in the Kosovo football league system and played its home matches at Hajvalia Stadium. It was known as a small but ambitious club that aimed to establish itself in the country’s top divisions.

During its competitive years, Hajvalia reached the Kosovo Superleague and also spent time in the First Football League of Kosovo, the second tier of the national system. The club gained attention for its rapid rise and for attempting to build a stronger squad compared to its modest infrastructure. One of its notable seasons came in the mid-2010s when it competed at the highest domestic level and faced some of the strongest teams in the country.

The club was dissolved in 2018 due to financial and organizational difficulties, ending its professional activities after nearly two decades of existence. Despite its short lifespan, FC Hajvalia is remembered in Kosovar football for its ambition and unusual media attention, including its widely publicized but symbolic attempt to sign global star Luis Suárez during his suspension period.

name: KF Malisheva
content:
KF Malisheva is a professional football club based in the city of Malishevë, Kosovo. The club was founded in 2016 and initially started as a youth football school before quickly developing into a competitive senior team. It plays its home matches at the Liman Gegaj Stadium and competes in the Kosovo Superleague, the top tier of football in the country.

The club’s rise has been rapid, progressing from the lower divisions of Kosovar football to the top level within a few seasons. After starting in the lower leagues, Malisheva earned successive promotions and reached the Superleague in the early 2020s. In its debut top-flight seasons, the club managed to establish itself as a stable competitor rather than a relegation candidate.

In recent years, KF Malisheva has also achieved notable results, including a strong league finish that qualified it for European competition for the first time in its history. This marked an important milestone for the club and highlighted its fast development within Kosovar football. Despite being a relatively young club, Malisheva is now considered a growing presence in the national football scene.
